'''Marilyn Olmstead''' (1943–2020) was an American chemist, an expert in small molecule [[crystallography]] and an international leader in the crystallographic study of [[fullerene]]s, or "Buckyballs." She held the position of professor emerita of [[chemistry]] at the [[University of California, Davis|University of California Davis]].<ref name=":5">{{Cite web|title=Marilyn Olmstead: My Life and Career in Chemistry {{!}} The Capitol Chemist|url=http://www.acs-sacramento.org/marilyn-olmstead-life-and-career-in-chemistry/|access-date=2021-08-14|language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Obituary: Marilyn Olmstead|url=https://cen.acs.org/people/obituaries/Obituary-Marilyn-Olmstead/98/i44|access-date=2021-08-14|website=cen.acs.org}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite web|date=2020-10-08|title=Remembering Professor Marilyn Olmstead|url=https://chemistry.ucdavis.edu/remembering-marilyn-olmstead/obituary|access-date=2021-08-14|website=UC Davis Chemistry|language=en}}</ref>

She was elected as a Fellow of the [[American Chemical Society]] in 2014<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|title=2014 ACS Fellows|url=https://cen.acs.org/articles/92/i28/2014-ACS-Fellows.html|access-date=2021-08-14|website=cen.acs.org}}</ref><ref name=":2">{{Cite web|date=2014-07-22|title=Three Alumni Named 2014 ACS Fellows|url=https://chem.wisc.edu/2014/07/22/three-alumni-named-2014-acs-fellows/|access-date=2021-08-14|website=Department of Chemistry|language=en-US}}</ref><ref name=":3">{{Cite web|date=2014-08-06|title=Women From Higher Education Named Fellows of American Chemical Society|url=https://www.wiareport.com/2014/08/seventeen-women-from-higher-education-named-fellows-of-the-american-chemical-society/|access-date=2021-08-14|website=Women In Academia Report}}</ref> and the [[American Crystallographic Association]] in 2017.<ref name=":4">{{Cite web|title=Fellows of the American Crystallographic Association|url=https://www.amercrystalassn.org/fellows|access-date=2021-08-14|website=www.amercrystalassn.org}}</ref>

== Early life ==
Marilyn Olmstead was born on December 8, 1943, in Glendale, California.<ref name=":0" /> and graduated from Burbank High School in 1961.

==Higher education==
Olmstead earned a B.A. in chemistry from [[Reed College]] in 1965. She attended [[University of Wisconsin–Madison|University of Wisconsin-Madison]] for her graduate studies, supported by a [[Woodrow Wilson Fellowship]]. She received her Ph.D. in chemistry from Wisconsin-Madison in 1969, the only woman in her graduating class of 40 students.<ref name=":5" />

== Career and discoveries ==
Olmstead started at the Department of Chemistry of the University of California, Davis in 1969 as lecturer in chemistry (1969–1975). She was subsequently appointed postdoctoral fellow (1971–1986), staff research associate (X-ray crystallography) (1986–1997), and specialist (1997–2003). By 2000, she was the in charge of a crystallographic laboratory that was one of the most productive in the world; she herself had the highest number of publications and cites of anyone in the chemistry department. Eventually, in 2003, when Marilyn was 60 years old, she was appointed to the faculty as full professor. She became a faculty member at the rank of professor Step 2 in 2003, and advanced through the system to professor, Step 6 in 2015.  She became emerita in 2015.<ref name=":0" />

Olmstead  was a specialist in small-molecule crystallography.  A focus of her research after 1990 was the structural characterization by [[X-ray crystallography]] of [[Fullerene chemistry|fullerenes]], both empty and filled ([[Endohedral fullerene|endohedrals]]) cages, in collaboration with  [[Alan Balch]]. Olmstead served as an original co-editor of the journal ''[[Acta Crystallographica Section E]]'' from 2001 to 2011. She  served in the elected positions of chair of the General Interest Group, and chair of the Continuing Education Committee in  the [[American Crystallographic Association]]. She was a member of the Journal's Commission of the [[International Union of Crystallography]]. She was an elected member of the U.S. National Committee on Crystallography, a branch of the [[National Academy of Sciences]].

In 2014 Olmstead was elected a Fellow of the [[American Chemical Society]].<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":2" /><ref name=":3" /> In 2017, she was elected a Fellow of the [[American Crystallographic Association]].<ref name=":4" />

==Death==
Marilyn Olmstead was killed on September 30, 2020, in a collision while cycling on a rural road north of Davis, California.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2020-10-01|title=Retired UCD chem professor killed while cycling on rural road|url=https://www.davisenterprise.com/news/local/cyclist-killed-on-rural-davis-road/|access-date=2021-08-14|website=Davis Enterprise|language=en-US}}</ref>
